issues.body:
Carried unchanged from rounds 1-3 at the same severity. sparq-wrapper-gen, sparq-wrapper-shacl and sparq-wrapper-integration are each a Cargo.toml with an empty `[dependencies]` plus a three-line `//!`-only lib.rs. Nothing depends on them and they export nothing, yet each is now built, clippy'd, doc'd and lock-resolved on every CI run.

The hygiene requirement from round 1 is met faithfully: each README carries the `<!-- internal-stub -->` directive, a one-line what/why and the `sq-1rg2q.1` bead marker; I re-confirmed gate-new-crate.py G1 PASS and check-readme-template.py 0 deviations across all 67 READMEs. This is residual cost, not a defect.

One cosmetic inconsistency with the sibling stubs persists: crates/sparq-crdt/Cargo.toml and crates/sparq-conformance-floors/Cargo.toml both set `readme = "README.md"` explicitly; the three new manifests omit it. Cargo auto-detects README.md in the package directory and the README template gate passes either way.
issues.fix_hint: If keeping them, state the reservation rationale in the PR body; optionally add `readme = "README.md"` to each of the three manifests to match the sibling stubs. If not, drop the three members (and their three Cargo.lock stanzas) and record each planned seam as a bead, creating the crate in the PR that implements it.
issues.title: Three empty crates join the workspace with no API, no dependents, and no consumer

issues.body:
The stale header sentence was already fixed in round 3 and remains count-free ("Implemented proposal features are default-OFF"), so the comment no longer drifts as features land. What remains is that proposed-async-events, proposed-async-node, proposed-async-store, proposed-graph-scope-events and proposed-json have no leg, so no CI lane ever builds them.

That is currently harmless: check-feature-test-execution.py's C1 guard only scans `crates/*/tests/**` files with an inner `#![cfg(feature = ...)]` plus `[[test]]`/`[[bench]]` `required-features` entries, and these five features gate no test target. Each gated module is a three-line doc-comment-only file, so a build of them could not fail. I also confirmed no gate in scripts/ enforces that every declared cargo feature has a matrix leg.

Caveat for this round: I could not re-run C1 (`scripts/check-feature-test-execution.py --check` aborts with "PyYAML is required" in this sandbox), so this rests on the round-3 source reading rather than a fresh execution.
issues.fix_hint: No change required now. Add each leg in the PR that lands the corresponding implementation and its tests, so C1 stays fail-closed the moment a gated test target appears.
issues.title: The five reserved features have no feature-matrix leg (harmless while the modules are empty)

issues.body:
Carried from rounds 2-3, unchanged. The PR ships crates/sparq-wrapper/docs/proposed/*.md and skills/rdf-wrapper/references/*.md — 24 files carrying the same eleven facts. They are complete and consistent in substance (I re-verified both indexes cover all 11 features with 0 unlinked pages and 0 dangling entries, and distinct.md is byte-identical in both trees), but the wording still diverges per page: docs/proposed/graph_scope_events.md says "Reserved implementation: `src/proposed/graph_scope_events.rs`" while references/graph_scope_events.md says "Reserved for a future implementation behind the default-off `proposed-graph-scope-events` feature". Every future proposal landing must touch both trees in lockstep; the round-2 omission of distinct from both indexes was an early instance of that drift.

Two layout points, both new convention rather than existing pattern: rdf-wrapper is the only skill in the repo with a `references/` subdirectory, and sparq-wrapper is the only crate with a `docs/` directory.
issues.fix_hint: Consider collapsing to one status table — a single section in skills/rdf-wrapper/SKILL.md, or one page listing all eleven features with a status column — and have crates/sparq-wrapper/README.md link to it, instead of 24 single-fact files kept in sync by hand.
issues.title: Two parallel status trees duplicate the same per-feature status in different wording

verdict.summary:
The round-3 blocker is genuinely closed. Verified at the PR head: [workspace].members yields 67 crates and all 67 now have a matching `name` entry in Cargo.lock (0 missing, 0 dupes). The three new stanzas sit in correct sort order between `sparq-wrapper` and `sparq-zk` (Cargo.lock:5825-5836) and are shape-identical to the dependency-less stub `sparq-conformance-floors` at Cargo.lock:4998-5000 — name + `version = "0.1.0"`, no `dependencies` key. `version.workspace = true` resolves to 0.1.0 (Cargo.toml:24); lock stays at `version = 4`. That removes the failure mode for build-matrix.yml:123-124, the five `cargo fetch --locked` steps in feature-matrix.yml, and supply-chain.yml:277,311.

Gates I could execute all PASS: gate-new-crate.py G1, check-readme-template.py (0 deviations / 67 READMEs), gate-api-skill.py G2, check-no-perf-numbers.py, check-terminology.py, coverage-presence.py --check (42 ok / 0 fail; the three publish=false zero-test stubs correctly not enrolled, matching the sibling stubs).

Docs are self-consistent. Every relative markdown link under skills/rdf-wrapper/** and crates/sparq-wrapper/** resolves: 0 broken; both status indexes have 0 unlinked page and 0 dangling entry across all 11 features. SKILL.md's new "Eleven" matches the 11 `proposed-*` features in Cargo.toml and the 10 `#[cfg(feature)] pub mod` lines plus module-less `proposed-distinct`, which is true against src/lib.rs:154-168 (inherent, feature-gated `subjects_of`/`objects_of`). Module sizes back "every other proposal feature is implemented": the five reserved modules are 3 lines each; the five implemented ones are 232-499.

No new dependency, no unsafe, no crypto/ZK/MPC surface, no hostile content, no perf claim.

Limitation: I could not compile (toolchain pinned 1.97.1, rustup dir read-only), and check-feature-test-execution.py --check aborts on missing PyYAML, so C1 rests on round 3's source reading. Only the carried minor and two nits remain — maintainer judgement, not defects.
